subject: Catalyst beta encoder — temporary uptime insurance request
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@catalysthealth.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Cc: lina.gomez@catalysthealth.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary uptime/latency commitment for beta encoder

Hi Chloe —

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re excited to move forward with the beta of Redwood’s new encoder (v0.9) for our clinical search pipeline. We expect to flip the feature to 10% of production traffic on Monday 9/6.

Before we proceed, our security and procurement teams are asking for a short-term written commitment on availability and latency. Specifically: an uptime target for the first 30 days and a 95th percentile token latency target for requests under 512 tokens. Because this is a preview model, we understand it may not meet regular GA SLAs — we’re open to a temporary carve-out/waiver if it’s documented and time-boxed.

Attached is a short form from procurement that outlines their ask (catalyst_uptime_request.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a time-boxed commitment or a fallback policy we can include in the change plan?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our product launch calendar is tight.

Best,
Samir
Director of Product
Catalyst Health

Attachments: catalyst_uptime_request.pdf

From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary uptime/latency commitment for beta encoder

Samir —

Thanks for sending this over and congrats on the upcoming launch. We can support a conditional, time-boxed commitment for the beta window with a few caveats:

- We can guarantee an operational target (not a contractual SLA) for 30 days: 99.0% availability for the encoder variant at the 10% traffic slice, and a 95th percentile token latency target of 280ms under typical load profiles (requests <512 tokens).
- This commitment is contingent on the rollout staying at or below 10% of total traffic and using the recommended batching and caching settings in our rollout guide.
- If we detect sustained degradation (latency > 350ms p95 or availability < 98.0% for 15+ minutes), automatic rollback to the stable model variant will be triggered.

I’m copying Rachel (Customer Success lead) and Ben (Sales Eng) to coordinate telemetry and the exact wording for procurement. I’ll also attach our standard temporary-waiver template for legal.

Proposed next steps:
1) Rachel to provide the monitoring hooks and a shared dashboard URL.
2) Ben to confirm recommended config for Catalyst’s traffic shape.
3) I’ll send a draft waiver that includes time window, metrics, rollback triggers, and escalation contacts.

We aim to get the draft waiver to you by end of day 9/2. Does that timeline work?

—Chloe
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: temporary_waiver_template.docx

From: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: chloe.martin@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary uptime/latency commitment for beta encoder

Hi Samir —

Quick note on monitoring and gating: we will provision a dedicated dashboard (read-only link) that surfaces per-model availability, p50/p95 latency, error rates, and autoscale events. For the beta window we recommend the following telemetry thresholds so both teams have clear triggers:

- Alert A (warning): p95 latency > 300ms for 10 consecutive minutes OR availability < 99.0% for 10 minutes.
- Alert B (action): p95 latency > 350ms for 15 consecutive minutes OR availability < 98.0% for 15 minutes — this triggers an automatic rollback rollback to the stable model.

We’ve attached a brief service-impact analysis (service-impact-analysis.xlsx) with sample traffic curves based on Catalyst’s submitted traffic profile. Ben — can you confirm the batching settings we discussed (max_batch_size=32, max_wait_ms=8) are safe for their traffic shape?

Samir — once you confirm the rollout percent and the time window (you mentioned 30 days), I’ll produce the dashboard link and invite your SREs to the monitoring channel.

Thanks,
Rachel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: service-impact-analysis.xlsx

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: chloe.martin@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, legal@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary uptime/latency commitment for beta encoder

Samir —

Thanks for the patience while we pulled the internal approvals together. Legal and Product Ops reviewed the proposal and can approve a 30-day temporary commitment with the following concrete language:

- Time window: 2026-09-06T00:00:00Z through 2026-10-06T00:00:00Z.
- Operational targets (time-boxed, not a permanent SLA): 99.0% availability and p95 token latency <= 280ms for requests <512 tokens when traffic remains at or below 10% of production.
- Rollback and failover: automatic rollback to stable model on Alert B conditions (p95 > 350ms for 15 minutes OR availability < 98.0% for 15 minutes).
- Reporting & audit: Redwood will provide daily summary telemetry and a final post-mortem if any Alert B events occur.

We’ve attached the signed temporary-waiver_template.docx and created the DocuSign envelope for Catalyst to sign (link below). Once the waiver is countersigned we’ll provision the dashboard, invite your SREs, and schedule a short go/no-go call 24 hours before the flip.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/agreements/0AB12345XYZ
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/12345

Please let us know who from Catalyst will sign the waiver and confirm the rollout timestamp (we’ve tentatively reserved 2026-09-06 09:00 PT).

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
